cards.title: wait
cards.summary: Pause execution until a time elapses, a condition becomes true, an event fires, or a reply arrives — discriminated by `attributes.type`.

meta.Hybrid / multi-path?: Hybrid — runs linear by default, becomes multi-path when `convertToMultipath: true`. Carries `isHybridAction: true` and `hybridActionType: "wait"` markers. See [`docs/04-workflow-anatomy.md §4`](../../10-anatomy/04-workflow-anatomy.md)
meta.UI editor source: No single recovered `.ts` file — split across `recovered-source/src/components/workflow/` and condition validators

fields.name: name
fields.notes: Required when populated; max length capped by `isWithinLimits`. 94.2%.

fields.name: startAfter
fields.notes: { type: "seconds" | "minutes" | "hour" | "days", value: number, when: "after" | ... }`. Required for `time`. 90.7%. The drawer's unit VALUES are `seconds`, `minutes`, `hour` (singular) and `days` — `startAfterTypeOptions` (Wait.ts:1588, bundle-2026-08-21-3) maps the plural LABEL "hours" to the value `hour`. The TS interface still declares `'minutes' | 'hours' | 'days'`, and stored workflows contain both spellings (`startAfter` blocks in corpus+sniffs: minutes ×71, days ×10, hours ×4, hour ×1) — so a stored `hours` was written by an API call, not the drawer. Whether the scheduler honours it is UNPROVEN; the engine accepts it with a warning.
